statement: The least squares objective is the sum of squared residuals—the differences between observed values and the values predicted by a model—to be minimized: S = \sum_{i} r_i^2 = \sum_{i} (y_i - f(x_i, \boldsymbol{\beta}))^2, where r_i = y_i - f(x_i, \boldsymbol{\beta}) is the residual for observation i; in matrix notation for linear regression models with dataset D, it is expressed as L(D, \boldsymbol{\beta}) = \|Y - X\boldsymbol{\beta}\|^2 = (Y - X\boldsymbol{\beta})^{\mathsf{T}}(Y - X\boldsymbol{\beta}) = Y^{\mathsf{T}}Y - 2Y^{\mathsf{T}}X\boldsymbol{\beta} + \boldsymbol{\beta}^{\mathsf{T}}X^{\mathsf{T}}X\boldsymbol{\beta}.

properties.property: Stationary condition: The minimum of the sum of squares is found by setting its gradient with respect to each parameter to zero: \frac{\partial S}{\partial \beta_j} = 2\sum_i r_i \frac{\partial r_i}{\partial \beta_j} = -2\sum_i r_i \frac{\partial f(x_i, \boldsymbol{\beta})}{\partial \beta_j} = 0 for j = 1, \dots, m.
properties.why: The extremum of a differentiable sum-of-squares objective occurs where all partial derivatives vanish.

properties.property: Normal equations for linear least squares: The gradient of the linear loss \frac{\partial L(D, \boldsymbol{\beta})}{\partial \boldsymbol{\beta}} = -2X^{\mathsf{T}}Y + 2X^{\mathsf{T}}X\boldsymbol{\beta} vanishes at X^{\mathsf{T}}X\boldsymbol{\beta} = X^{\mathsf{T}}Y, yielding the closed-form solution \hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = (X^{\mathsf{T}}X)^{-1}X^{\mathsf{T}}Y = X^+ Y.
properties.why: The linear least squares objective is quadratic in \boldsymbol{\beta}, producing a linear system of gradient equations with an explicit algebraic inverse.

properties.property: Gauss–Newton normal equations for non-linear models: Linearizing f(x_i, \boldsymbol{\beta}) via a first-order Taylor expansion about current iterate \boldsymbol{\beta}^k with Jacobian J yields iterative updates via (J^{\mathsf{T}}J)\Delta\boldsymbol{\beta} = J^{\mathsf{T}}\Delta\mathbf{y}.
properties.why: Nonlinear models generally have no closed-form solution and require iterative local linear approximations.

properties.property: Tikhonov regularization (ridge regression): Adds an \ell_2-norm penalty \alpha \|\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_2^2 to the residual sum of squares objective.
properties.why: Formulates a constrained minimization on parameter magnitude into unconstrained Lagrangian form, equivalent to placing a zero-mean normal prior on \boldsymbol{\beta}.

properties.property: Lasso regularization: Adds an L1-norm penalty \alpha \|\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_1 to the residual sum of squares objective.
properties.why: Imposes an L1-norm constraint on the parameter vector, equivalent to a zero-mean Laplace prior.

properties.property: Convexity and uniqueness: Linear least squares is globally concave (convex) with a unique solution, whereas non-linear least squares may possess multiple minima.
properties.why: The objective Hessian is constant and positive semidefinite (X^{\mathsf{T}}X) for linear models, but parameter-dependent and non-convex in nonlinear models.

assumptions.assumption: Errors have expectation zero conditional on independent variables, are uncorrelated, and have equal variance (homoscedasticity)
assumptions.breaks_when: Residual variance depends on the predictor x_i (heteroscedasticity) or errors are correlated, violating the Gauss–Markov theorem conditions.

assumptions.assumption: The normal equations matrix X^{\mathsf{T}}X is invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: Predictor variables are linearly dependent (multicollinearity) or the number of parameters exceeds the number of observations (m > n).

assumptions.assumption: In non-linear least squares, initial parameter values \boldsymbol{\beta}^0 are sufficiently close to the global optimum
assumptions.breaks_when: Poor initial parameter guesses lead the iterative solver to non-convergence or to entrapment in suboptimal local minima.

failure_modes.signature: Iterative algorithm fails to terminate or find a parameter update satisfying the stopping threshold
failure_modes.cause: Non-linear least squares objective surface is non-convex and lacks global convergence guarantees.

failure_modes.signature: Algorithm converges to parameter values yielding an unexpectedly large residual sum of squares
failure_modes.cause: Nonlinearity in parameters creates multiple stationary points in the sum of squares objective.
Columns of design matrix X are collinear or the system has fewer observations than unknowns.

failure_modes.signature: Residual plot exhibits a fanning-out pattern towards larger or smaller Y_i
failure_modes.cause: Variance of the dependent variable depends on the predictor variable x_i rather than remaining constant.
